statement: Fix 1 ≤ n < d, c > 0, 0 < G < ∞, 0 ≤ D0 < ∞, and 0 < γ < 1/2. Let µj be Radon measures on Rd with 0 ∈ Ej = supp µj, global upper n-growth G, and µj(B(x, r)) ≥ crn (x ∈ Ej, 0 < r ≤ diam Ej). Assume every hard-truncated Riesz transform on L2(µj) has norm at most D0. Let δj > 0, integers Kj ≥ 0, and Aj, vj > 0 satisfy δj −→ 0, Kj −→ ∞, δj2γKj −→ 0, 2Kj ≤ diam Ej, Aj −→ ∞, vj −→ 0. (3.15) 25 Suppose eµj (0, 2k ) ≤ δj2γk (0 ≤ k ≤ Kj) (3.16) and |Rµj (φ)| ≤ vj if Lip φ ≤ 1, supp φ ⋐ B(0, Aj), Z φ dµj = 0. (3.17) There is a subsequence, relabeled by j, with the following properties. All the input sequences are restricted along this same subsequence when we relabel them. For each index there are an affine plane Sj = aj + Lj(Rn), tangent and normal linear isometries Lj : Rn −→ Rd , Nj : Rd−n −→ Rd , LjL∗ j + NjN∗ j = I, such that aj is the point of Sj nearest 0, aj → 0, and Lj → L∞ in operator norm, where L∞ is an isometry. Along this same subsequence, µj ⇀ q(L∞)#Ln , c 4nωn ≤ q ≤ 2nG ωn , ωn = Ln (B(0, 1)). (3.18) Here convergence is against continuous compactly supported tests, and Ln in (3.18) denotes Lebesgue measure. The planes obey (3.6) with a single constant M = M(n, d, c, G, γ). In particular, writing ei for the standard basis of Rd−n and uj,i(x) = ⟨Njei, x − aj⟩, (3.19) we have Z B(0,2k) |uj,i|2 dµj ≤ Mδ2 j 2k(n+2+2γ) (0 ≤ k ≤ Kj, 1 ≤ i ≤ d − n). (3.20) Moreover, on every bounded ball, the supports converge bilaterally to L∞(Rn): each source support point approaches that plane uniformly, and each point of the plane approaches Ej uniformly.
